   page when you pick one. The state a sighted player reads off the ring is
   carried for everyone else by the chip's `.equip-chosen-note`. */
.poker-equipment-choice.on > .equipment-choose { visibility:hidden; pointer-events:none; }
/* The gold `.poker-equipment-choice.on` outline that used to sit here is
   GONE ON PURPOSE (#997): it was this picker's own invention, and the chosen
   state is now the one green ring the whole game shares, drawn on the card's
   own face by `.is-chosen` above. `.on` stays on the CHIP because the rule
   just above still needs it to quiet the button. */

/* Creation keeps card nodes in place so focus can lift and settle smoothly.
   ONE PLACEMENT, AND THE ROOM IT NEEDS (Constantine's review, 2026-09-12).
   The information badge hangs above a selected card on every surface, this one
   included; a corner exception here read as a second rule for the same
   control. What made the exception necessary was room, not placement — with
   nothing reserved the badge straddled the STARTING ARMOUR header's border
   (measured 1280x800, 2026-09-11) — so these selectors reserve it: the 64 px
   row gap every other card scrollport keeps, and a head that is DERIVED from
   the badge it has to clear, floored at the 80 px this rule used to type.
   THE HEAD IS THE BADGE'S OWN RISE, READ FROM THE BADGE'S OWN TOKENS.
   Nothing declares --card-info-size any more, so the control here is the shared
   circle, and main.js writes its size and hang onto the document root from
   wireframeUi.inspect (--inspect-size, --inspect-gap). --cc-choice-rise reads
   those same two properties through the same var chain the button's own `top`
   uses, so a config change moves the head with the badge instead of past it: at
   sizeRem 4 / gapPx 20 the badge grows to 67.2 px and the old head, which had
   the 2.75 and the 10 typed into it, clipped 17.3 px (measured 2026-09-14).
   The third term is the focus lift — translateY(-6px) plus the 5 % of the
   card's height that scale(1.05) about center bottom grows upward, 20.2 px of
   layout at UI size S — which is what the 26 covers, with slack.
   A head derived from --tap-floor was tried and refused, and the max() floor is
   why: that token divides by a zoom that runs ABOVE 1 on a desktop (1.48 at
   1920), and a head that shrinks with it clipped 8 px off the first row there
   while the badge had not moved. This expression only ever GROWS the head, and
   it resolves to exactly 80 px at every zoom of 1 or more, so the Auto sizes
   keep the geometry measured above.
   THE ROW GAP RIDES THE SAME TOKEN, and keeps the 64 every other card
   scrollport keeps wherever the head is at its floor. A second row's badge
   overlaps the row above by design — it is drawn over that card at z-index 8,
   measured 2.9 px into it at 1280 with the default tokens — so the gap is not
   full clearance and is not what keeps a badge whole. Deriving it only stops a
   bigger badge from deepening that overlap: the gap grows by exactly what the
   head grows, never less than 64.
   The floor alone was not enough: at UI size S (--ui-zoom 0.85) with NORMAL
   motion the badge's top sat 0.8 px past the scrollport's padding box at every
   desk width measured — 1280, 1366, 1440 and 1920 (2026-09-14; ui-sweep's
   fixture asks for reduced motion, which drops the lift, so R5 could not see
   it, and the row now runs a second pass that can). Derived, the head is
   89.53 px there and the same cells clear by 7.3 px; 390 at Auto (zoom 0.9)
   takes 86 px and clears by 18.1.
   Measured whole and clear of the section face at 1280, 1366, 1440, 1920 and
   390, at UI sizes Auto, S, M and XL, under normal motion.
*/
/* The derived head belongs to the SCROLLPORT, not to one of its two layouts:
   the badge hangs above a selected card in either view, and in either view the
   first row is the one that would push it onto the section face. So the two
   custom properties and the group placement sit on the container itself and
   both `data-view` branches read them. */
.cc-equip-group > .cc-card-selectors { --cc-choice-rise:calc(var(--inspect-size, calc(2.75 * max(16px / var(--ui-zoom, 1), 1rem))) + var(--inspect-gap, calc(10px / var(--ui-zoom, 1))) + 26px); --cc-choice-head:max(80px, var(--cc-choice-rise)); grid-row:1 / span 2; }
.cc-equip-group > .cc-card-selectors[data-view="grid"] { padding:var(--cc-choice-head) 6px 14px; gap:calc(64px + var(--cc-choice-head) - 80px) 12px; grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(132px,1fr)); align-content:start; }
.cc-card-selectors[data-view="grid"] .poker-equipment-choice { position:relative; min-width:0; width:100%; justify-self:center; padding:4px; }
/* FOUR CHOICES IN THE GLASS, NOT TWO (2026-09-12). Constantine: "cards are
   too big. I should easily be able to see 4 cards on this screen." Measured
   before this rule, the Main Hand choices column showed exactly two cards at
   every desktop size (1366x768: a 497x505 scrollport holding 228x371 cards;
   1440x900: 548x600 holding 252x412; 1920x1080: 703x710 holding 326x529) —
   the column was pinned to two tracks, so a wide pane bought bigger cards
   rather than more of them. The track count above is therefore unpinned and
   the card is browsing-sized at 152px; the reading is the detail pane's job
   and the art is the inspect modal's.
   THE HEAD AND ROW GAP ABOVE ARE NOT PART OF THAT SAVING. This branch also
   removed them, on the premise that the information badge sat inside the
   card's corner and the head was reserving nothing. That premise no longer
   holds: the badge hangs ABOVE a selected card on every surface, and the head
   is what keeps the first row's badge off the section face. So the derived
   head and gap stand exactly as they are, and only the track count and the
   card cap come across.
   Choose appears below the selected card, in its own reserved action slot. */
.cc-card-selectors[data-view="grid"] .equipment-choose { position:static; width:100%; margin-top:10px; }
.cc-card-selectors .equipment-poker-card { position:relative; z-index:1; transform-origin:center bottom; transition:transform 180ms ease-out, box-shadow 180ms ease-out; }
.cc-card-selectors .choice-focused .equipment-poker-card { transform:translateY(-6px) scale(1.05); z-index:3; box-shadow:0 12px 26px #0008,0 0 18px #d0ac5d55; border-radius:12px; }
.cc-card-selectors .equipment-choose { white-space:normal; overflow-wrap:anywhere; line-height:1.2; padding:6px 4px; font-size:14px; }
/* Retain the action slot so browsing does not move the next row under a pointer. */
.cc-card-selectors[data-view="grid"] .poker-equipment-choice:not(.choice-focused) .equipment-choose { visibility:hidden; pointer-events:none; }

/* ═══ THE SAME CHOICES AS A LIST ══════════════════════════════════════════
   Grid, above, is a browsing wall: the card is shrunk to 152px, the Choose
   button follows its foot in a reserved action slot, and both it
   and the information badge are hidden until a card is focused — everything
   bought back is spent on fitting more cards in the glass (#996).
   List makes the opposite trade and is the honest counterpart the toggle
   never had. One card per row at a readable 108px beside a text column, so
   the name and the Choose button are legible WITHOUT focusing first, and the
   action is a plain block in the flow rather than an overlay: a row has the
   height to hold it, so hiding it would buy nothing. Row count, not card
   count, is what a list is for.
   The card keeps its lift on focus — that is the picker's focus language and
   it reads the same in either view. */
.cc-card-selectors[data-view="list"] { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:10px; padding:var(--cc-choice-head,80px) 6px 14px; align-content:start; }
.cc-card-selectors[data-view="list"] .poker-equipment-choice {
  position:relative; display:grid; grid-template-columns:var(--card-w-glance-compact, 108px) minmax(0,1fr); gap:12px;
  align-items:center; width:100%; min-width:0; max-width:none; padding:8px;
  border:1px solid var(--line-soft, #5e4c32); border-radius:10px;
}
.cc-card-selectors[data-view="list"] .poker-equipment-choice.on { border-color:var(--gold, #c9a227); }
/* The list view sets its cards beside their own text, so it reads a narrower
   width — `sizing.levels.glance.variants.compact` in card.json, not a number
   invented here. The TRACK above reads the same token, so the column and the
   card it holds cannot disagree; a literal there would cap whatever the card
   asked for, which is how the shop's oversized frame happened (#1167).
   THE VIEW DECIDES THIS WIDTH, NOT THE LEVEL, and keying it on `[data-level]`
   was wrong: `levelForView('list')` returns `focus` (src/model/cardFields.js),
   so EVERY card in this view is `focus`, selected or not — measured in the
   real picker, not inferred. A `[data-level="glance"]` key therefore matched
   nothing here and the rule was dead on its only surface.
   That is also why writing it unconditionally does not bring back the defect
   it was keyed to avoid: nothing in this view promotes on selection, so there
   is no card here that this cap would hold at a resting size. The level still
   chooses the FIELD SET the card shows — which is the whole point of a list
   row, name and effects legible beside the card — while the view chooses how
   wide it is drawn. */
.cc-card-selectors[data-view="list"] .equipment-poker-card { width:100%; transform-origin:center left; max-width:var(--card-w-glance-compact, 108px); }
.cc-card-selectors[data-view="list"] .equipment-choose {
  position:static; width:100%; margin-top:0; min-height:var(--tap-floor); font-size:14px;
}

/* WHAT AN UNFOCUSED CHIP WITHHOLDS IS AUTHORED NOW, NOT HAND-ROLLED HERE.
   A `:not(.choice-focused) .card-info-button { visibility:hidden }` rule stood
   here: one screen's private flag, in CSS, for the one field anybody had got
   round to hiding. That is the mechanism the presentation levels replace —
   `content/config/ui/components/card.json` says what each of glance / focus /
   inspect shows, `src/model/cardFields.js` answers it, and the face does not
   render what it is not saying. A second copy of that decision in a selector
   is exactly the drift Law 1 is about, so the rule is gone rather than kept
   "just for the button". */
/* The catalogue's three-level specimen: FLOW ONLY. Each face is sized by the
   picker rules above, because how big a card is has one home and this is not
   it; all this adds is that the three stand side by side under their names. */
.cc-card-levels { display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; align-items:flex-start; }
.cc-card-levels > .cc-card-level { margin:0; }
.cc-card-levels > .cc-card-level > figcaption { text-align:center; text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:.06em; color:var(--muted); }
.cc-equipment-details { max-width:none; }
.cc-equipment-details h3 { margin:0 0 8px; }
.cc-choice-context, .cc-package-context { color:var(--muted); font-size:14px; line-height:1.4; margin:0 0 12px; }
/* THE SUBSTEP'S WAY ON OUTRANKS THE STAGE'S SKIP.
   The stage row above (`.cz-stage .modal-btnrow.end`) is pinned to the
   scrollport floor at `z-index:2`, and this button is right-aligned in the same
   band. MEASURED at 1366x768 with Main Hand open: scrolled so `Continue to Off
   Hand` reaches the floor, the two overlap by 46.9px vertically and 203.7px
   horizontally, and `elementFromPoint` at this button's own centre returned
   `BUTTON.as-btn cz-next` — the player pressing the section's Continue was
   reaching `Continue to seed`, SKIPPING the armament they had come to choose.
   Below 700px the sticky rule further down already answers this with
   `z-index:3`; above it this button is a static grid item, so it lost the paint
   order to a later, positioned sibling. A grid item's containing block is its
   own one-row grid area, so it cannot be made sticky here (the reason the
   sticky rule is mobile-only) — but it does not need travel, only rank.
   `position:relative` with no offsets moves nothing and changes no layout; it
   only lets the z-index apply. */
.cc-equipment-continue { grid-column:2; grid-row:2; justify-self:end; align-self:end; min-height:44px; max-width:100%; white-space:normal; position:relative; z-index:3; }
/* The ready lift scales the button about its centre, and at the grid's right
   edge that is a 2px horizontal overflow (measured: section scrollWidth 1100
   against clientWidth 1098 at 1024 wide). Growing from the right edge keeps
   the lift inside the section. */
.cc-equipment-continue, .cz-next, .cc-primary-continue { transform-origin:100% 50%; }
/* Ready, the label is bold, and bold "Continue to equipment" ran 2px past the
   long button's box at 1440 wide (measured: scrollWidth 210 in a 208 box).
   Less side padding than the row's clamp gives it, so the words stay whole. */
.cz-next { padding-inline:clamp(0.5rem, 5%, 1rem); }
/* AND THE ROW GIVES THE WORDS THE ROOM, because the padding alone could not.
   Creation's physical text floor (`.customize :is(..., button)`, 16px over the
   zoom) outranks the ButtonRow's fit-to-box type clamp, so the label does not
   shrink into a `long` row: "Continue to character" wanted 227px of that row's
   208px box at 1280x720 and ellipsed to "Continue to chara...". The step's way
   on is one button alone on its row, so the row is sized to the longest of
   those labels instead of the shared `long` step. */
.as-btnrow:has(> .cz-next), .modal-btnrow:has(> .cz-next) { --step: 26rem; }
/* THE WAY ON NEVER SCROLLS OUT OF REACH (Constantine, 2026-09-12: *"the
   continue button always in view and not requiring too much scrolling"*).
   MEASURED: with the right-hand section open at 390x844 the creation scroll is
   2129px against a 784px viewport, and the section's Continue sits at the end
   of it. A player who had chosen scrolled back through everything to leave.
   STICKY RATHER THAN MOVED TO THE FOOT, and the reason is the hooks: `#cz-start`
   and `.cz-next[data-next]` are read by startup-gate, character-creation-check
   and the contact sheet, and the foot is `.cz-actions`. Relocating the buttons
   changes what every one of those instruments walks. Sticky changes where the
   same button PAINTS and nothing about where it lives, so the fix costs no
   instrument a re-teach.
   The row carries its own ground: a transparent sticky control with the stage's
   content sliding under it is unreadable at the moment it matters. */
.cz-stage {
  /* How far above the scrollport's floor a SECOND sticky row has to rest, so it
     clears the first. Authored once because CSS cannot ask how tall a sibling
     is — but DERIVED, not typed, because every part of that height is a setting
     the player can move:
        var(--tap-floor)  the button inside the row, which is
                          `calc(var(--tap-target) / var(--ui-zoom, 1))` — it
                          grows with Minimum tap size and with Auto's zoom
        12px              the row's own `padding-block: 10px 2px`, below
        10px              the scrollport's `padding-bottom`, which is why the
                          stage row's painted bottom sits above the floor
                          rather than on it
     THIS WAS A CONSTANT AND THE CONSTANT WAS WRONG. 64px measured clean at the
     default 44px target, and collided again as soon as the target moved: at
     `--tap-target: 60px` the rows overlapped by 8px at zoom 1 and by 27.8px at
     zoom 0.62. A number that only holds at one setting is a number that has
     not been derived. */
  --cz-continue-row: calc(var(--tap-floor) + 22px);
}
.cz-stage .modal-btnrow.end,
.cz-stage .cc-primary-continue-row {
  position:sticky; bottom:0; z-index:2;
  background:linear-gradient(to top, var(--panel) 62%, transparent);
  padding-block:10px 2px; margin-block-start:8px;
}
/* TWO WAYS ON CAN BE STICKY AT ONCE, AND THEY MUST NOT SHARE THE BAND.
   The character stage holds both: the nested `Continue` that closes Primary
   Stats and opens the Keepsake, and the stage's own `Continue to equipment`.
   MEASURED at 390x844 with Primary Stats open, both rested at exactly
   top 693 / bottom 748 — the same 55px band, the same z-index — so the stage
   row, later in the DOM, painted over the nested one. What a player saw at the
   bottom of the glass was the DISABLED `Continue to equipment`, with the
   actionable control hidden underneath it.
   Both are needed: with the nested row made static it falls to 828, which is
   71px below a band that ends at 757, so it cannot simply stop being sticky.
   So they STACK — the nested row rests one row higher, and paints above, which
   also keeps it legible while the two pass each other on a scroll.
   The selector carries `.modal-btnrow` because the nested row wears `end` too,
   and would otherwise lose the specificity contest with the rule above. */
.cz-stage .modal-btnrow.cc-primary-continue-row {
  bottom:var(--cz-continue-row); z-index:3;
}
/* A fold's summary is a control: it takes the tap floor and the kit's ring.
   THE FLOOR IS THE TOKEN, NOT THE NUMBER. `--tap-floor` is
   `calc(var(--tap-target) / var(--ui-zoom, 1))` precisely because `body` carries
   `zoom: var(--ui-zoom)`: a literal 44px below body renders at 44 x zoom, so at
   Auto's 0.62 floor this control would have been a ~27px physical target while
   every button beside it stayed 44. The division cancels the zoom; the number
   does not. The comment said "takes the tap floor" while the code took a
   constant that happens to equal it at zoom 1. */
.cc-starting-fold > .cc-starting-summary {
  display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; align-items:baseline; gap:4px 10px;
  min-height:var(--tap-floor); padding:10px 4px; cursor:pointer; list-style:none;
}
.cc-starting-fold > .cc-starting-summary::-webkit-details-marker { display:none; }
.cc-starting-fold > .cc-starting-summary::after {
  content:'\203A'; margin-inline-start:auto; color:var(--muted);
  transition:transform 150ms ease-out;
}
.cc-starting-fold[open] > .cc-starting-summary::after { transform:rotate(90deg); }
.cc-starting-fold > .cc-starting-summary b { color:var(--gold); }
.cc-starting-fold > .cc-starting-summary .cc-package-context { margin:0; }
.reduced-motion .cc-starting-fold > .cc-starting-summary::after { transition:none; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .cc-starting-fold > .cc-starting-summary::after { transition:none; }
}
/* INSIDE THE FOLD THE CARDS ARE A REFERENCE, AND ARE DRAWN AS ONE. The
   renderer's `small` flag was the wrong tool and is not used here: its only
   effect is `transform: scale(0.92)`, which `.cc-starting-card > .card` above
   correctly cancels — a transformed card still occupies its untransformed box,
   so it saves no scroll at all. A smaller BOX does. Three to a row instead of
   two turns six faces from three rows into two. */
.cc-starting-fold .cc-starting-card-grid { grid-template-columns:repeat(3,minmax(0,1fr)); gap:9px 7px; }
.cc-starting-fold .cc-starting-card { padding-top:34px; }
.cc-starting-fold .cc-starting-card > .card { max-width:104px; }
.cc-starting-fold .cc-starting-card .card-info-button { top:-36px; }
.cc-starting-package { margin-top:20px; border-top:1px solid var(--line); padding-top:16px; }
.cc-starting-package h4 { margin:0 0 8px; color:var(--gold); font-size:18px; }
.cc-starting-card-grid { display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr)); gap:11px 9px; }
.cc-starting-card { min-width:0; display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:center; gap:6px; padding-top:42px; }
.cc-card-quantity { font-size:13px; color:var(--gold); align-self:start; }
.cc-starting-card > .card { width:100%; max-width:150px; height:auto; aspect-ratio:var(--card-ratio); min-width:0; margin:0; transform:none; }
.equipment-poker-card[data-item='empty-hand'] .epc-art-glyph { font-size:92px; line-height:1; color:var(--gold); }
.cc-starting-card .card-info-button { top:-44px; }
/* CARD LORE — the identity line in inspection and the lore modal behind it
   (components/loreLine.js). The player picks the face, size, spacing and slant
   under Advanced → Text & lore; models/LoreTypeModel.js writes the choice on
   <html> as data-lore-* words and the rules below turn words into type. The
   faces are bundled (assets/fonts/, CREDITS.md) under their own "AS Lore"
   names, so none of them changes the game's headings or body text. The lore
   window sizes in rem against the 62.5% root (1rem = 10px at Text M); the
   inspection line is 1.6rem (16px at Text M, so Text size grows it) with the
   card-inspection pane's zoom floor, the same in playing-card and equipment
   inspection. */

/* THE CLASS STEP FITS THE GLASS ON DESKTOP (2026-09-12).
   Constantine: "continue button is cut off". The step's one way on — its
   "Continue to character" — stood below the door's foot at EVERY desktop size
   measured, because the split grows to its content inside a scrolling body and
   the Continue row is the last thing in that column:

     1280x720   glass 477px, step 598px, Continue at y=725, foot at y=621
     1366x768   glass 515px, step 628px, Continue at y=762, foot at y=666
     1512x860   glass 584px, step 694px, Continue at y=842, foot at y=752
     1920x1080  glass 737px, step 859px, Continue at y=1044, foot at y=946

   Same cure as THE OPEN EQUIPMENT SECTION below, one step later in the same
   flow: the split is capped to what the door body leaves under the step's own
   face, and its two panes scroll INSIDE that cap — the class list and the
   preview each own their overflow — so the Continue never leaves the glass.
   The subtraction is the same one, for the same reason: the door's head and
   foot, the step face and the panel's breathing room, over the zoom (the
   chrome measured 23.2-24.5rem across the four sizes above, so 25rem is the
   conservative floor for all of them). The `max()` keeps a short window from
   collapsing the split to nothing — under it the body scrolls as it did.
   Below the split's own stacking width the phone layout stands: chooser first,
   preview after it, the page scrolling as one. */
@container (width > 64rem) {
  .cc-class-split { max-height: max(30rem, calc(100dvh / var(--ui-zoom, 1) - 25rem)); grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr); }
  .cc-class-split > .as-split-pane { min-height: 0; }
  .cc-class-split > .as-split-pane > .as-pane { min-height: 0; overflow: hidden; }
  .cc-class-split > .cc-class-preview-host > .as-pane { overflow-y: auto; scrollbar-gutter: stable; }
  .cc-class-split .cc-choice-collection { flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto; scrollbar-gutter: stable; }
}
/* THE OPEN EQUIPMENT SECTION FITS THE GLASS ON DESKTOP (2026-09-11).
   Constantine: "the screen is slightly too big, i should be able to see
   everything when it opens on desktop." Measured at 1366x768 before this
   rule: the Main Hand section stood 1423px tall — the card-package preview in
   the detail pane — with its Continue at y=1707 on a 768px glass. The section
   is capped to what the door body leaves under the section's own face, and
   its two columns scroll INSIDE that cap: the choices column and the detail
   pane each own their overflow, so the Continue never leaves the glass. The
   subtraction is the door's head and foot, the section face and the panel's
   breathing room, divided by the zoom for the reason .modal's ceiling is.
   The choices scrollport's head (above) is what keeps the above-card inspect
   control off the section face on the first row. Phones keep the stacked,
   page-scrolling layout below. */

/* THE WAY ON IS ON THE RIGHT; THE WAY BACK IS ON THE LEFT. Constantine,
   2026-09-11: "progression buttons should be on the right, and back buttons
   should be on the left". `modalFooter()` already builds the row in that
   order — every secondary, then the one primary — and `.modal-btnrow` lays it
   out as equal grid tracks, which is the owner's earlier rule from
   2026-09-03: "make primary and secondary buttons at the bottom uniform in
   size" (tools/modal-shell-contract.mjs asserts those equal tracks). So a
   ready primary needs NOTHING here but the full width of the foot to divide.

   IT USED TO TAKE MORE THAN THAT, AND THAT IS WHAT PUT IT ON THE LEFT. The
   block replaced the ladder's tracks with `grid-template-columns:repeat(2,
   minmax(0,1fr))` and gave the primary `grid-column:1 / -1; order:1`,
   intending a full-width row of its own. Grid does not place it that way: the
   ordered item takes the explicit two-track span, the auto-placed secondary
   is pushed into an IMPLICIT third track, and the line reads primary-then-back
   from the left. Measured at 1280x800 before this change — creation's foot
   computed `grid-template-columns: 383.47px 383.47px 383.47px`, Begin at x=10
   spanning 842px and Back at x=854; the title's slot picker did the same with
   Continue at x=424 and Back at x=717.

   A FLEX ROW IS NOT THE FIX EITHER, measured rather than assumed: the ladder's
   buttons carry `min-width:0` with an ellipsis, so a primary on `flex:1 1 auto`
   shrank Back to a 32px box with the word gone — on both surfaces, and
   `flex:0 0 auto` on the secondaries did not bring it back. The tracks stay;
   only the overrides go. The emphasis this block was written for is the
   primary's colour, lift and focus ring above, none of which moved. */
.modal-foot-actions:has(> .primary:not([hidden]):not(:disabled):not([aria-disabled='true']):not([data-confirm-ready='false'])) {
  width:100%; margin-left:0;
}
.modal-foot-actions > .primary:not([hidden]):not(:disabled):not([aria-disabled='true']):not([data-confirm-ready='false']) {
  max-width:none; min-width:0;
}
/* A lone exit (pile, flask, combatant door) lost `.primary` with its role;
   it still spans the foot it is the only way out of. */
.modal-foot-actions:has(> [data-control-role='exit']:only-child) { width:100%; margin-left:0; }
.modal-foot-actions > [data-control-role='exit']:only-child { max-width:none; min-width:0; }
/* THE CREATION FOOT KEEPS BACK LEFT AND BEGIN RIGHT once Begin is ready. The
   stacked ready-primary foot above is for a door whose primary is the one
   thing left to do; here Back is a real way out, and Constantine (2026-09-11):
   "continue and done etc confirmation buttons should be on the right, and
   back buttons on the left". Scoped to this foot; every other door keeps the
   stack. */
.modal-foot.cz-actions:has(> .modal-foot-actions > .primary:not([hidden]):not(:disabled):not([aria-disabled='true']):not([data-confirm-ready='false'])) {
  flex-direction:row; align-items:center;

   are the same shape as each other:
   1. The two-column rule pinned the art track to the authored inspect width
      and sat AFTER the `max-width: 600px` collapses further up this file —
      same specificity, later in source — so it won at every width. On a 390px
      phone the card took 320 and the details took a sliver.
   2. The first fix for that repeated the mistake one level down: its mobile
      overflow rules sat BEFORE `.modal-body { overflow: hidden }` and
      `.card-inspection-details { overflow-y: auto }` just above, so the
      details stayed an inner scrollport and the body stayed clipped. The
      promised single scroll was not what shipped. Copilot caught it on #1162.
   Hence its position here: after everything it has to beat.

   THE THRESHOLD IS NOT A NUMBER IN THIS FILE. A media query cannot read a
   custom property, so an earlier draft wrote `calc(20rem + 24rem)` and called
   it derived — it was a second copy of the inspect width that would not have
   moved when card.json did. `cardInspectionLayout()` in

   the authored readable measure and sets `data-card-door`, so the one home

   four of the five pages that host this layout never load. */

/* WCB0 BUTTON SIZES. Every value comes from wireframeUi.buttons through
   ButtonSizeModel.buttonSizeTokens(), written onto :root by the kit; this
   block only combines them. A reference rem is at least 16 physical px (the
   hand and footer plans' unit), so heights neither shrink with the zoom nor
   with the 10px root. Widths belong to the group that owns the action region:
   the footer above divides it into equal shares after the shared gap (a sole
   action fills it); a choice row gives every sibling one preset of the row,
   capped by the equal share, and wraps labels rather than sizing to them. */
:root {
  --button-reference-rem: max(calc(16px / var(--ui-zoom, 1)), 1rem);
  --button-gap: calc(var(--button-gap-rem, 0) * var(--button-reference-rem));
  --button-minimum: calc(var(--button-minimum-rem, 0) * var(--button-reference-rem));
}

button[data-button-size$='-double'] { --button-height-multiplier: var(--button-height-double); }
